companyDescription: AI Memory · HBM4/HBM3E leader with sold-out capacity through 2026 — the picks-and-shovels memory play behind every AI accelerator
priceNote: Trading $1,021.28 (+6.91%), rebounding within a $976-$1,213 range after pulling back from the Jun 25 all-time high of $1,213.37. Up over 250% YTD on sold-out HBM capacity and the Anthropic AI partnership.
summary: Micron's Jun 24, 2026 Q3 FY26 print was a blowout — EPS $25.11 vs $20.20 est (+24%), revenue $41.46B vs $35.84B est, and FQ4 guidance of ~$50B revenue vs $43.2B consensus — yet the stock has pulled back ~16% from its Jun 25 all-time high on profit-taking and the broader AI-semis selloff. Consensus target ~$1,486 (45 analysts) implies ~46% upside from the current $1,021.28. HBM capacity is sold out through 2026 with long-term supply agreements locking in ~40% of revenue through 2028-2030. Next earnings (Q4 FY26) land Sep 29, 2026.

catalysts.name: Q4 FY2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Tests whether the ~$50B FQ4 revenue guide (vs $43.2B Street consensus at the time) actually lands, and whether HBM4 volume ramp (already exceeding $1B revenue) continues accelerating into fiscal 2027.

catalysts.name: HBM4 Volume Ramp for NVIDIA Vera Rubin
catalysts.description: Micron has begun volume shipment of HBM4 12-Hi designed for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform — directly tied to NVDA's H2 2026 shipment timeline, with HBM4E volume production targeted for calendar 2027.

catalysts.name: Anthropic Strategic AI Partnership
catalysts.description: Long-term supply agreement supporting the AI memory demand story — part of 16 long-term agreements totaling $22B in locked-in revenue.

risks: Stock is up over 250% YTD and ~16% off its all-time high — even after the pullback, a lot of good news is already priced in, raising the bar for the Sep 29 print
Micron itself said it can only fulfill 50-66% of some key customers' HBM demand in the medium term — a supply constraint that caps near-term upside even as it validates pricing power
SOX-wide 'buyer exhaustion' concern — the Jul 2026 selloff hit Intel, AMD, and Micron alongside AVGO, suggesting sector-level de-rating risk independent of MU's own results
Memory is historically the most cyclical semis sub-sector; the current HBM supercycle narrative assumes sustained AI capex that some analysts (BofA Bubble Risk Indicator 0.91) view skeptically
Hawkish Fed dot-plot shift pressures long-duration AI-capex multiples independent of MU execution
Next earnings (Sep 29) is the furthest out of any near-term semis catalyst in this dashboard — more time for sentiment to swing before the next hard data point

estimateDates.note: Key test: does FQ4 revenue hit the ~$50B guide, and does HBM4 ramp momentum continue into fiscal 2027

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held 3.50–3.75% for a 4th straight meeting (Jun 17, 2026). Next FOMC Jul 28–29 — CME FedWatch prices ~89% probability of another hold, but the June dot plot raised the median 2026 rate projection, now leaning toward a hike rather than a cut.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation still running above the 2% target; the hawkish dot-plot shift removes a rate-cut tailwind AI/growth names had been pricing in.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: High-multiple AI/semis names are the most rate-sensitive part of the market — a hawkish surprise compresses long-duration growth multiples faster than it hits earnings, adding to the cyclicality risk already inherent in memory stocks.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — no imminent hike, but a hawkish surprise at the Jul 28-29 FOMC would compound both the sector-wide capex-fear selloff and memory's structurally higher cyclicality risk.

postWin.note: Jun 24, 2026 (Q3 FY26): stock rose 15% in extended trading after EPS beat consensus by 24.3% ($25.11 vs $20.20) and FQ4 revenue guidance ($50B) blew past the $43.2B Street estimate — the clearest, most recent comparable for this exact catalyst type.

postLose.note: No recent MU-specific miss on record this cycle — the closest analog is the current ~16% pullback from the Jun 25 all-time high, which was profit-taking and sector rotation rather than a company miss, but shows how fast sentiment can reverse even after a blowout print.

spotSizing.reason: BUY verdict with Strong Buy consensus and ~46% upside after a genuine ~16% pullback from all-time highs following a beat-and-raise quarter — size at 6% initial, add on further dip toward $900-950 given memory's higher cyclicality than logic semis.
